title: Tenant Spend Splitter: priority bands for region & GPU profile selection
creator: Priya Patel
description: Implement a tenant-facing routing controller ("Tenant Spend Splitter") that divides inference traffic into priority bands and selects region + instance class (spot vs on-demand, GPU profile) according to per-tenant budget caps and SLA preservation policies. The controller should make probabilistic routing decisions when capacity is constrained, enforce soft and hard spend caps, and gracefully direct requests to lower-cost model variants or degraded quality paths when budget constraints require it.
technical_design:
Core components:
- Band allocator: per-tenant priority bands (P0..P3) compute routing weights based on recent spend velocity, configured budget windows, and SLA priority tag.
- Instance selector: maps a routing decision to a concrete region and accelerator class (A100, H100, L4, etc.) and precomputed model variant (full precision, 8-bit quantized, distilled).
- Spend guard: enforces soft caps (signal for throttling/variant substitution) and hard caps (reject or queue). Uses tokenized accounting and a sliding-window spend ledger per tenant.
- Hedging & probabilistic fallback: when on-demand capacity limited, probabilistically route a fraction of P0/P1 traffic to spot or secondary regions with retry/hedge windows to maintain p95 latency SLA.
- Telemetry hooks: emit per-request routing decision, expected unit-cost delta, and spend counters for audit + billing reconciler.
Implementation notes:
- Controller runs in control plane with fast-path caching (TTL 5s) for tenant policy and last-known capacity hints; decisions are sent as immutable routing tokens to the data plane.
- Use backfill experiments in dev cluster to calibrate probability thresholds and variant quality delta (A/B evals).
- Keep routing policy DSL small: mapping {tenant, priority, remaining_budget_pct, recent_spend_rate} -> band weights + allowed_instance_classes + variant_set.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator: deterministic workload replay shows spend capped within +/-10% of target across 1, 7, 30 day windows for 95% of tenants
SLA: P0 path maintains p95 latency within configured SLO for >= 99% of requests during normal load in integration test (no more than 2% degradation vs baseline)
Fallback correctness: when budget triggers, at least one lower-cost model variant is used and end-to-end response shape remains JSON-parseable and passes smoke QA prompts
Observability: dashboards showing per-tenant spend, band distribution, percent routed to spot/on-demand, and model-variant usage are populated and tested
Rollout recipe: feature flagged by tenant and can be rolled back per-tenant within 10 minutes

Implement band allocator service and unit tests
Implement spend ledger (token-based) and integration tests with billing mock

2026-02-27 Miguel Santos: Prototype band allocator implemented; initial unit tests for spend ledger added. Observed that bursty traffic causes overspend in naive sliding window - need exponential damping.

2026-03-03 Eng QA: Integration test with billing mock shows soft caps trigger substitution to quantized variants successfully but introduced 120ms median latency in region failover path; investigating caching of routing tokens to eliminate extra lookup.
2026-03-07 Data Science: Suggested adding expected quality delta metric per prompt class to the decision heuristic; this will allow targeted substitution where hallucination risk is low.
